sentences.text: "Greg" Peters is co-chief executive officer and president of Netflix, Inc., a position he has held alongside Ted Sarandos since January 2023, when he stepped up from chief operating officer and joined the Netflix board as part of the succession from co-founder Reed Hastings.

sentences.quote: In 2008, Peters joined Netflix as the company's international development officer, responsible for global partnerships with consumer electronics companies, internet service providers, and multi-channel video programming distributors.
sentences.text: He previously served as chief operating officer and chief product officer, and earlier as international development officer for Netflix, having joined the company in 2008 as international development officer, responsible for global partnerships with consumer electronics companies, internet service providers and multi-channel video programming distributors.

sentences.quote: Prior to joining Netflix in 2008, he was Senior Vice President of consumer electronics products for Macrovision Solutions Corp.

citations.title: Netflix to lay off roughly 1,000 employees, or 6% of workforce

sentences.quote: Netflix co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters wrote in the email to employees
sentences.text: Netflix remains led by co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters.

On October 14, 2026 they told staff of roughly 1,000 job cuts, about 6% of the workforce, with product, tech, legal and human resources most affected, saying the mission requires discipline about where people and resources are prioritized and that the business remains on track for the full-year forecast.
Days later the company named former Disney and Fox executive Peter Rice chief content officer from October 26, replacing Bela Bajaria after ten years.

sentences.quote: Executive chairman Reed Hastings, the company's co-founder who served as CEO for 25 years and drove it to become the world's leading premium streamer, officially departed the Netflix board following the June 4 annual shareholders meeting.
sentences.text: Co-founder Reed Hastings became non-executive chairman in April 2025 and left the board after the June 4, 2026 annual meeting, with Jay Hoag appointed chairman.
